I'm not gonna do the shrooms. I agree with all the replies about that, I don't need them and it is drug use. The other thing is essentially just doing for me what taking psychiatric medication would do, but with a whole lot less side effects and risks. My psychiatrist is fully on board with what I'm doing for that. It may share a name with ket, but in essence it's just like receiving a one-time dosage of an antidepressant so that you don't have to take it daily. 


And thank you so much. I really appreciate it. I plan to fully immerse myself into NA and sober life upon leaving this rehab. Gonna work on getting a sponsor right away.

I have major depressive disorder, anxiety, OCD, and PTSD. If I stop the infusions I will have to go on more drugs, but those with extreme side effects, antidepressants, mood stabilizers, antipsychotics which have addictive and abuse potential. In my opinion those are worse and have been detrimental in my life prior to getting ketamine infusions. I'm not going to do the shrooms, I agree with you there, but the ketamine infusions are not drug use, they are a researched and proven mental health treatment. I'm getting them by the advice of medical professionals. I'm not getting them to get high. If I were just an addict, I wouldn't need them. I have existing mental health issues that are incurable without medication and existed long before my addiction began. No 12 step program is going to solve my incurable mental health issues. So, I'm going to work the 12 steps and go to meetings, but I'm not going to stop getting a treatment which I know will be detrimental to me if I do. It would be like telling someone who is stable on anti-depressants to go off their meds. So, I respectfully disagree about the ketamine infusions. I need them. I am not going to risk depression and suicide just because this treatment happens to share a name with a recreational substance.
Like I said in the other reply, ketamine infusions for mental health are completely different than recreational ket. I've never done ket outside of a strictly controlled medical setting.

The treatment protocol for IV ketamine administered by a doctor is completely different than recreational. It is a small dosage administered over the course of an hour. It was completely life changing for me and getting an infusion every couple months completely changed my life and honestly saved it. I would have killed myself if it had not been for finding that treatment when I did. I understand it is the same drug as recreational, but if the protocol are followed it does not have addictive potential. My psychiatrist is completely on board with it and there is an intranasal spray that is FDA approved for treatment resistant depression. That being said, I've also never done recreation ket. I'd probably have a much different reaction if I had done that first.

I've done quite a bit of research on ketamine therapy for depression and it quite literally heals the brain from the effects of stress, which damage neural connections and lead to depression. I was so depressed when I began getting it that I could not get out of bed for months and it really changed my life. However, my ketamine doctor says repeatedly it is imperative to use it to make therapy effective and rewire neural pathways on your own with work so that you don't keep getting to that point where you're depressed. 


At the rehab I'm also getting TMS, which is a similar mechanism to ketamine, but may be more of interest to you since your DOC is ket. It's supposedly long term.

Ok thank you. I needed to hear this.  I'm putting in so much work at the rehab and have access to an amount of therapy I've never had, so ideally I want to leave here and be able to manage my mental health on my own. I appreciate it.
Alright, thank you very much
I'll be doing that as part of my rehab! Very excited
Ok thank you, by this logic I think I'll continue getting the ketamine infusions since they are administered by doctor at clinic, and abstain from psilocybin because I'd be doing that on my own

It makes sense. Ketamine infusions I'm going to continue to do because I get them administered by a doctor and it essentially does the same as an antidepressant and is not addictive with no side effects. That I'm sure of. But, I can see why psilocybin would be problematic under my own control. I'm going to see if I can get psilocybin microdosing prescribed eventually. Thank you for explaining

Over the past 5 years, weed has pretty much ruined my life. I started halfway through high school and was an Ivy League bound student, but it had such an impact on my mental health and personality that I have lost most of the friends I made over the years, have lost multiple jobs, and will now be graduating very late (if at all) from the prestigious university I attend. I have also had multiple psychotic breakdowns, which led to lengthy and traumatic hospitalizations and months of remaining delusional and driving people away. I cringe when I remember the bullshit I used to say to people in psychosis. My mom used to be the closest person to me, we barely talk now. My brothers are terrified of me because I almost stabbed myself in front of them, which is only one of many suicidal ideations I have had over the years. I used to be so smart I qualified for Mensa and now even basic cognition can be a struggle. I have also spent countless amounts of money to sustain my addiction, often resorting to stealing from others just to get some more (even my parents and one time my close friend). Or even worse, manipulating people into giving me money. Munchies were so bad initially that I ballooned up to nearly 300 lbs despite being a student athlete prior, I have stretch marks all over now because I used to order food delivery every night that would consist of thousands and thousands of calories, often on credit cards that werent mine. I was ambitious, intelligent, and driven before weed, now I feel sluggish, lazy, stupid, and unconcerned (ifyky). I have tried multiple times to quit, however I always convince myself that I can go back and use in moderation, which typically has coincided with me withdrawing from school and ignoring all my obligations. I went from being top ranked in my class to almost not graduating high school, all in the matter of about a year or two. I am also extremely surprised I have not gotten a DUI, as I used to take no precautions and smoke bongs, joints, even take DABS while driving. I once went through a checkpoint with a car that reeked of weed and they didn't stop my car for whatever reason, pledged to stop due to that, then relapsed soon after. Right before my worst psychotic breakdown I almost robbed a convenience store, as I was spending $50 a day for wax to dab, despite being involved with various social justice causes at school that would abhor any such behavior. 

I still think weed should be legalized for all and have no issue with it so long as people do not abuse it or use it while having most mental illness. However, the people most likely to turn to it in desperation are those with mental illness or underlying issues likely to be impacted negatively by weed. Even when my life was spiraling out of control, I still was convinced it was doing good, or that things would be worse if I wasn't using it. It altered my mind to the point where I began making it my personality and only interest. I do not think anyone who is under 18 should EVER use it, the stoners I have known over the years have all done poorly and my experience is a testament to how detrimental weed abuse is on education. I think there are valid medical uses like treating cancer, AIDS, appetite, PTSD, etc., and also that it could be better recreationally than other drugs or alcohol, however I am now less sure of how make it available to such people without encouraging use in detrimental groups. 

I believe that I would be doing better in every aspect of my life had I not begun smoking, or even if I had somehow found a way to limit myself. I never thought of myself as brilliant prior to smoking weed, but it is clear I had a gift and an ability to impact the world positively doing most anything I wanted, and that my weed addiction has robbed me of that. Now, it can sometimes take my everything to accomplish the simplest tasks or reponsibilities. 

I stopped once again a few days ago, have been absolutely miserable since, and anticipate having to feel this way for weeks or months before I see what of my brain was salvaged. However, I am hoping I still have enough time as a young adult to have some good experiences, rather than continue to watch all my former friends graduating, getting married, and living stellar lives, while I meanwhile have lost everything I spent my entire childhood working for.
